RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 0

Both you and the successful candidate are men, making it virtually impossible that sex discrimination influenced the hiring decision between the two of you. While an all-male panel may reflect broader institutional diversity shortcomings within the hospital's leadership, it did not place you at a gender-based disadvantage.

The decision likely hinged on the successful candidate's formal management training and broad leadership experience versus your technical research background. Raising the panel's gender composition would appear unfounded and could damage your professional credibility. Instead, send a polite follow-up to HR or the hiring lead requesting constructive feedback on how you can strengthen your leadership profile for future executive appointments.
